title: Operational Resilience: Stakeholder Scenarios & Vettable Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a lightweight, vettable playbook for validating Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and running cross-functional resilience scenarios with product, infra, and support stakeholders. The goal is to provide a repeatable, low-friction path from hypothesis -> tabletop simulation -> tuned SLOs -> monitored rollout.

Audience:
- Service owners (product engineers)
- Platform & infra teams (serving-runtime, platform-engineering)
- Site Reliability engineers and Ops
- Customer Success and Support

High-level approach (one-line):
Run short, measurable experiments that exercise SLO assumptions across both traffic and failure modes, capture stakeholder impact statements, and produce a small catalog of mitigations and policy decisions that can be automated or operationalized.

Sections in this doc:
1) Quick decision canvas for SLO vetting
2) Three scenario templates for tabletop & live simulation
3) Scoring rubric and acceptance criteria
4) Communication & escalation matrix
5) Rollout phases and owners (playbook checklist)
6) Open questions and follow-ups

1) Quick decision canvas for SLO vetting
- Service: short id (e.g., chat-generation-v2)
- Primary user impact: latency vs correctness vs availability
- Candidate SLOs (examples): p95 latency, availability (successful responses), error-rate by class, downstream dependency availability
- Business tolerance: quantified in minutes of degraded UX or dollar impact per hour (fill in)
- Capacity sensitivity: high | medium | low
- Fallback options available: cached responses, smaller model variant, degraded feature flag
- Acceptance criteria for staged rollout: defined in scoring rubric below

Template (fill during workshop):
- Service: ____________________
- Product owner: ____________________
- Proposed SLOs: ____________________
- Key dependencies: ____________________
- Rollout window: ____________________

2) Scenario templates (keep them short; can be used for tabletop or synthetic load)
A. Latency storm (traffic surge + batch behavior)
  - Trigger: 3x normal traffic for 10 minutes with 50% of requests having longer sequences (+50 tokens)
  - Aim: verify batching and autoscale behavior, observe p95/p99 latency, and queue/backpressure interactions
  - Stakeholders: serving-runtime, platform-engineering, product
  - Success signals: p95 within target, no cascading queue growth, alerts hit on expected thresholds
  - Mitigations to validate: dynamic batching adjustment, route-to-fallback, autoscaler scale-up speed

B. Dependency degradation (downstream embedding store partial outage)
  - Trigger: 30% of embedding store requests return 500 or time out for 15 minutes
  - Aim: measure end-to-end error-rate and user-visible correctness impact; ensure graceful fallback to cached or approximate embeddings
  - Success signals: service-level error-rate under budget, degraded-correctness metrics captured, customer-impact note drafted
  - Mitigations to validate: KV cache warm paths, local fallback, degrade ranking tolerance thresholds

C. Model variant failover (model OOM / node losses)
  - Trigger: simulated loss of 1/3 of GPU capacity in a region for 20 minutes while maintaining normal traffic
  - Aim: test routing policies, automatic fallback to quantized or smaller model, and per-customer tier behavior (dedicated vs hosted)
  - Success signals: graceful performance degradation for free-tier traffic, reserved capacity for enterprise routes preserved, no data-plane errors leaking
  - Mitigations to validate: smart routing rules, priority rescheduling, surge protection

3) Scoring rubric & acceptance criteria (score 0-3)
- Latency (0: p95 > 2x target; 1: p95 slightly above; 2: within target most of time; 3: within target)
- Correctness/User Impact (0: major regression; 1: noticeable but acceptable; 2: minor; 3: negligible)
- Observability (0: blind spots; 1: partial signals; 2: good metrics; 3: full traces/alerts)
- Recovery speed (0: manual only; 1: partial automation; 2: mostly automated; 3: fully automated fallback)
- Triaged runbook (0: none; 1: partial; 2: clear steps; 3: rehearsed)

Pass thresholds (example): overall >= 10/15 and no 0s in latency or correctness. If not passed, list required fixes and repeat scenario within 2 weeks.

4) Communication & escalation matrix
- Pre-sim: 72h notice to impacted teams + CS for customer-aware services
- During sim: dedicated Slack channel + SRE bridge owner (name/rotation)
- Post-sim: 48h write-up in shared drive + short async blameless retro 3 working days after
- Escalation paths: page on P0 if user-facing errors exceed 1% for 15 minutes; otherwise normal oncall flow

Stakeholder quick references:
- Product: define business tolerance and customer-critical flows
- Infra/Platform: validate autoscale/contingency knobs; confirm capacity runbook
- SRE: author & own the tabletop script; capture telemetry gaps
- CS/Support: prepare customer-facing template if outage crosses threshold

5) Rollout phases & playbook checklist (minimal viable path)
Phase 0 — Hypothesis & Metrics (owner: service PO)
  - Define SLO candidates and failure modes (documented in canvas)
  - Map dependencies and their SLOs (downstream stores, third-party APIs)
  - Small telemetry smoke tests to ensure metrics emit (p50/p95/p99, error categories)

Phase 1 — Tabletop (owner: SRE lead)
  - Run 1-hour tabletop with stakeholders; fill decision canvas
  - Identify immediate mitigations and telemetry gaps
  - Update runbook & playbook draft

Phase 2 — Synthetic & Canary (owner: platform eng)
  - Run scenario on staging with synthetic traffic and wired-in failures
  - Validate metrics and automated fallback behavior
  - Canary to small percentage of production traffic if staging passes

Phase 3 — Gradual rollout (owner: service PO + SRE)
  - Incremental rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48–72 hours with close monitoring
  - Stop criteria defined by scoring rubric and error budgets

Phase 4 — Post-rollout retro & sloset (owner: SRE)
  - Postmortem-like retro; capture lessons and update central SLO catalog
  - Schedule quarterly re-checks or after large infra changes

Playbook checklist (pre-sim):
- [ ] Canvas filled
- [ ] Alert thresholds and dashboards created
- [ ] Oncall rota assigned and notified
- [ ] Customer comms template ready (if needed)

6) Tabletop script (short)
- 00:00 — Quick context & objectives (5 min)
- 00:05 — Walk through decision canvas for service (10 min)
- 00:15 — Trigger scenario specifics; ops team simulates alert flows (20 min)
- 00:35 — Stakeholder impact statements: product, CS, infra (10 min)
- 00:45 — Triage and mitigation plan (10 min)
- 00:55 — Capture action items and owners (5 min)

7) Live simulation runbook notes (for infra/platform to use)
- Keep simulations non-customer facing by default. Canary small internal accounts first.
- Use traffic generators that can reproduce sequence-length distributions (not only QPS) — important for model-serving systems.
- Pause automation if unknown failure modes appear; prefer manual diagnose then re-run once understood.
- Record all runs and keep telemetry artifacts for 90 days (metrics, traces, sampled requests).

8) Capacity & cost scenario matrix (short prescriptive guidance)
- If SLO requires <50ms p95 under normal load, costs tend to be 2–3x baseline for reserved capacity — tradeoff doc required for product sign-off.
- For high-frequency short requests, prioritize batching tweaks; for long-sequence workloads, prioritize kernel and KV cache optimizations.
- Recommendation: include a simple cost-card in the canvas (estimated $/hour for three failure modes)

9) Decision log template (use for each sim)
- simulation_id: YYYYMMDD-service-short-id
- run_owner: name
- outcome: pass | partial | fail
- score: numeric from rubric
- actions: comma-separated short items with owners and due dates

Open questions & TODOs (short list):
- How do we automatically map error budget consumption to customer SLA comms? (Action: Lina to prototype mapping, due 2027-01-20)
- Validate synthetic traffic fidelity for customers using long-context inputs (Action: Marco to share generator config, due 2026-12-01)
- Define a light-weight approval gate for canary that product can sign off quickly (Action: Product leadership to propose)

Appendix — Useful snippets and templates (copy-paste friendly)
- Example canary stop criteria: error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes OR p95 > 1.5x target for 15 minutes
- Customer-facing outage blurb (template): "We’re investigating degraded performance for [feature]. We have mitigation measures and expect partial restoration within X hours."

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc intentionally short. Link to canonical SLO catalog in Confluence and avoid duplicating long definitions here.
- Next iteration: add a lightweight automation checklist for toggling fallbacks via feature flags and an autoscaler playbook snippet.

Last updated by Rohan Patel on 2027-01-08 — draft for partner review.
